body:
Publishing a new blog post via emily blog post immediately 403'd for real visitors. Root cause: the live iduna process's own actual umask (checked via /proc/<pid>/status: 0027, not systemd-managed -- runs as a ~/.config/systemd/user/iduna.service unit with no UMask= directive) silently turned every os.MkdirAll(0o755)/os.Create() call in internal/blog/render.go into on-disk 0750/0640, world-unreadable to nginx, while every older post stayed 0755/0664 from whenever it rendered under a different ambient umask. RenderPost/RenderIndex/RenderManifest now explicitly os.Chmod to 0755/0644 after creation, independent of process umask. Verified live: published a real post (brawlpit-alphastar-league, chmod'd by hand to unblock immediately), restarted iduna via systemctl --user restart iduna (clean health check), published a throwaway verification post that landed correctly permissioned with zero manual chmod, then cleaned it up (DB row deleted, rendered dir removed, index/manifest re-rendered via the real blog package -- confirmed gone from /blog/, blog-manifest.txt, and returns 404). Commit IDUNA 887734b.

⚓ ☃
title: S458: fix blog post permissions (ambient umask silently made new posts world-unreadable)
